themes_detail.label: Graffiti Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints surged to 26 this week versus a historical average of 0.9 per week—a 2,871% spike (z-score: 27.1)—signaling either a sudden coordinated tagging campaign or a critical breakdown in removal response across East Flatbush.
evidence: 26 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2,871% increase)
Z-score of 27.1 indicates extreme statistical anomaly—far beyond normal variation
No corresponding spike in graffiti removal or enforcement actions identified in public data
reporting_angles: On-the-ground visual survey: map the graffiti hotspots and document tag patterns (organized crew vs. random tagging)
Sanitation Department response time: how long does removal take, and is the city understaffed?

themes_detail.label: Street Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints jumped to 54 this week compared to an 8-week baseline of 11.6 per week—a 364% spike (z-score: 7.84)—suggesting widespread pothole, pavement, or sidewalk failures emerging in real time.
evidence: 54 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 11.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (364% increase)
Z-score of 7.84 indicates highly significant statistical deviation
318 total DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (173 alterations) may indicate construction-related street damage
reporting_angles: Photo essay: identify the worst streets, measure pothole depth, document traffic hazards
DOE/DOT responsibility: are construction projects going unpermitted, or is scheduled maintenance backlogged?

themes_detail.label: Electrical System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints spiked to 4 last week versus a historical average of 0.1 per week—a 3,100% increase (z-score: 11.72)—potentially indicating widespread wiring failures, overloaded circuits, or fire hazards in residential buildings.
evidence: 4 electrical complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3,100% increase)
Z-score of 11.72 confirms high statistical significance
Electrical failures pose immediate fire and safety risk to residents
reporting_angles: Safety investigation: interview FDNY on electrical-related fire calls in the district over the past 2 weeks
Building compliance audit: check Con Edison service disruptions and whether buildings are upgrading aging infrastructure

themes_detail.label: Sanitation & Cleanliness Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dirty conditions spiked to 47 complaints two weeks ago (185% above the 16.5-week average) and residential disposal complaints hit 7 last week (144% above 2.9-week average), indicating an emerging waste management or street-cleaning failure across the neighborhood.
evidence: Dirty condition complaints: 47 two weeks ago vs. 16.5 weekly average (185% increase, z-score: 3.9)
Residential disposal complaints: 7 last week vs. 2.9 weekly average (144% increase, z-score: 3.54)
Convergence of two related sanitation categories suggests systemic issue, not isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Street-level reporting: document uncollected trash, overflowing bins, and rat activity in target blocks
Sanitation scheduling: interview DSNY about collection schedule changes or staffing reductions in CD 317

themes_detail.label: Tree Health & Environmental Decline
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints jumped to 3 last week from a baseline of 0.5 weekly—a 500% spike (z-score: 3.54)—signaling accelerating tree mortality potentially linked to climate stress, disease, or inadequate maintenance.
evidence: 3 dead/dying tree complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (500% increase)
Z-score of 3.54 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Small absolute numbers limit trend robustness but warrant monitoring
reporting_angles: Urban forestry check-in: speak with NYC Parks about the cause of recent die-offs in the district
Climate resilience angle: is East Flatbush losing canopy due to heat, drought, or pest pressure?
